transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-08-20
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Lena Park (Redwood AE), Marco Diaz (Redwood SE), Priya Menon (CTO - Aerocart), James Li (Eng Lead), Sofia Ramos (Security), Tom Becker (Product)

Summary: quick discovery focused on PLG quickstart vs reserved/dedicated private hosting. Customer worried about data residency, KMS/HSM, and cost/latency tradeoffs. Redwood AE/SE explained hosted API, dedicated reserved pools, and private VPC options. Agreed to pilot with free credits and run a perf benchmark; security pack to be shared.

00:00 Lena Park: hi everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Lena from Redwood Inference, i'm the AE on the account, with me is Marco, our solutions engineer. today we wanted to understand your goals for the quickstart and the deployment fit - hosted, dedicated or private, right?
00:12 Priya Menon: yep, thanks Lena. i'm Priya, CTO at Aerocart. short context: we want to ship a conversational search feature inside our merchant dashboard. primary concerns are data privacy for merchant PII, predictable cost, and keeping latency below 300 ms p95 for typical queries.
00:28 James Li: hi, James here — eng lead. we've tried a couple of open-source runtimes in-house but the ops burden is high. looking at Redwood because it says 'production-first' and we like the idea of quickstart credits to get to first token.
00:43 Marco Diaz: great, quick note — we provide a hosted API for fastest time-to-first-token (TTFT), dedicated reserved GPU pools for predictable throughput and a private option with VPC and on-prem. we can do canary rollouts, A/B tests, and fallback to smaller models for graceful degradation.
01:05 Sofia Ramos: hi, Sofia, security. my team needs to know about data retention, KMS integration, and audit logs. SOC 2 is checkbox one, but we also need to know whether logs contain user request payloads and how long they persist.
01:18 Lena Park: understood. Marco, can you cover the security package briefly?
01:22 Marco Diaz: sure. we have SOC 2 type 2, ISO is coming on request, we support SAML SSO and RBAC, audit logs are available via the console — you can configure retention. for keys we integrate with customer KMS and HSM, though in the hosted plan we by default manage keys unless you opt for private with customer-managed KMS. apologies if I said H M S earlier, it's HSM.
01:45 Priya Menon: so in hosted is the data ever stored in plain text logs?
01:50 Marco Diaz: by default request logs are captured for debugging and can be redacted; for customers that need zero persistence we recommend private deployment or Dedicated with log redaction policies — you can also opt out of request retention entirely.
02:05 Tom Becker: product question — how does the TTFT actually work? what's in the quickstart?
02:12 Lena Park: quickstart typically includes an API key, starter example repo, and free credits. for Aerocart we'll offer a 90-day pilot with free credits to run your integration and initial evaluation. that gets you to first call same day in most cases.
02:28 James Li: do we need code changes for a later move to Dedicated or Private?
02:32 Marco Diaz: minimal. same API surface — we keep SDK and REST interface consistent. switching deployment modes is primarily config + credentials and possibly model pinning. some infra networking changes for VPC/private but the code paths are 95% identical.
02:45 Priya Menon: good — that reduces lock-in worries. cost is still a concern. can you speak to token pricing differences between hosted and dedicated?
02:53 Lena Park: hosted is usage-based per token; dedicated is a reserved capacity contract — you pay for the GPU pools plus a lower per-token execution charge. for sustained high throughput Dedicated often saves money, but reserved commits needed. we'll send modeled scenarios.
03:10 Sofia Ramos: for regulatory reasons, some of our merchants need data to stay inside EU. do you have region controls?
03:16 Marco Diaz: yes, region routing is supported. Hosted API can route to specific regions and we have private deployments we can stand up in EU regions or on-prem for strict residency. if you need a VPC deployment, that's our Private offering with customer-controlled networking.
03:32 James Li: on latency — we're aiming for 300 ms p95. what are typical latencies for a 2k token context with a 70B-ish model?
03:39 Marco Diaz: typical numbers vary, but for a 70B quantized model on our optimized serving runtime you can expect 150-400 ms depending on batch and cache. continuous batching helps, and prefix/KV cache yields big wins for multi-turn chat. we'll benchmark with your workload.
03:56 Priya Menon: we'd like to test with our query mix and some doc retrieval. can the pilot run vector embeddings and reranking too?
04:03 Marco Diaz: yes, embeddings + reranking + generation are supported via the Redwood API. we can include an evaluation script that runs embedding + search + rerank per query during the pilot.
04:18 Tom Becker: security again — what's the model for encryption at rest?
04:21 Marco Diaz: encryption at rest is standard with customer-managed KMS available on Private and Dedicated, hosted by default uses Redwood-managed keys but we can support customer KMS for enterprise customers.
04:33 Sofia Ramos: do you have attestation for HSM on the hosted side?
04:36 Marco Diaz: hosted doesn't have dedicated HSM attestation per tenant; that's available with Private where you bring your own HSM or we configure a dedicated KMS integration.
04:49 James Li: what does the pilot look like practically — how long, what's the success criteria?
04:54 Lena Park: pilot: 4–8 weeks ideally. Redwood provides 90 days of credits but we usually aim 4 weeks of active test + time for analysis. success criteria we recommend: integration complete, latency within your p95 target for X% of queries, and cost per 1k queries below threshold. we can co-define metrics.
05:14 Priya Menon: ok, timeline is tight — merchant trial in mid-october — so must have pilot wrapped by late september.
05:21 Lena Park: that's doable. we'll push to get bench scheduled early Sept.
05:25 Marco Diaz: quick note on fallback — if Dedicated capacity is saturated we can route to hosted variants of the same model automatically, so you don't go down; it's part of our graceful degradation policies.
05:40 Tom Becker: curious about model variants and quantization — how many pre-quantized variants do you host?
05:45 Marco Diaz: we maintain several quantization profiles per model and pick kernels based on hardware and sequence length. sometimes model names get scrambled in transcripts but we deploy verified variants tuned for latency/cost tradeoffs.
05:58 James Li: is there an audit trail for model rollouts?
06:02 Marco Diaz: yes, Console has rollout history, which model versions were live, canary performance metrics, and automatic rollback triggers.
06:12 Priya Menon: ok, let's talk about integration effort — we have a Next.js admin and a Go backend. can we route calls from backend directly?
06:20 Marco Diaz: absolutely. REST or SDKs work fine. you'll typically call Redwood from your backend; we recommend a server-side token, not embedding it in frontend.
06:29 James Li: do you support rate limiting and quotas per API key or per route?
06:33 Lena Park: both. per-key quotas, per-route token limits, and you can set rate limits at the org or team level.
06:40 Sofia Ramos: more on logs — will the console show raw prompt text? we need to redact sensitive fields automatically.
06:46 Marco Diaz: we offer configurable redaction rules and PII scrubbing; for maximum control use Private where you can disable retention completely and keep logs in your S3/KV store behind your VPC.
06:58 Priya Menon: do you provide usage cost breakdowns by token or by route?
07:02 Lena Park: yes — Console gives token-level cost and latency breakdowns per route and model. we can also surface per-endpoint dashboards or export the data to your SIEM.
07:13 Tom Becker: we might want canary some merchants vs all — are rollouts tied to accounts?
07:18 Marco Diaz: you can route by customer ID, region, or tag. rollouts are flexible — canary percent, AB, and automatic fallback based on error rates.
07:29 James Li: from an ops perspective — how do you do capacity planning for Dedicated? how elastic is vertical scaling?
07:36 Marco Diaz: Dedicated offers reserved pools plus configurable autoscaling policies and a burst option. if you need strict latency SLOs, we recommend a commit sized for peak plus autoscale to cover unexpected spikes.
07:50 Priya Menon: ok we want to see costs. can you sketch a scenario?
07:54 Lena Park: we'll run a cost model: your estimated QPS, average tokens per call, and target p95 latency. Marco will prepare a few scenarios: hosted-only, mixed (hosted + dedicated with fallbacks), and private.
08:10 James Li: about compliance — do you do penetration tests and share reports?
08:14 Marco Diaz: we do third-party pen tests and can share redacted reports under NDA.
08:20 Sofia Ramos: will you share the data flow diagram for Private?
08:24 Lena Park: yes, that's part of the security pack we'll email.
08:29 Priya Menon: on the free credits — are there limits to what we can run in the pilot? e.g., GPU benchmarks, continuous load tests?
08:36 Lena Park: credits can be used for integration, eval, and benchmarks. for heavy stress testing we coordinate so it doesn't affect other customers; we can provision a pilot pool for your benchmark windows.
08:48 Tom Becker: any gotchas moving from self-serve to dedicated regarding model licensing?
08:52 Marco Diaz: some open models have license clauses; we verify model usage and help with model onboarding. for proprietary models you might host them in Private.
08:59 James Li: how are embeddings priced?
09:02 Lena Park: embeddings are per-unit at a different rate than generation tokens; we'll include per-embedding pricing in the pricing sheet.
09:10 Priya Menon: let's lock the pilot dates — Sep 1st bench and Sep 6–30 active trial?
09:16 Lena Park: sounds good, we'll propose Sept 1st 10:00 UTC for the 2-hour benchmark.
09:21 Marco Diaz: I'll send the benchmark script plus an example dataset and a small harness you can run locally.
09:27 Priya Menon: wonderful. one last item — we sometimes sign via procurement with a PO and an annual contract; what is typical lead time for Dedicated procurement?
09:36 Lena Park: procurement time varies; once you commit, setup for Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) can be as fast as 2–4 weeks for standard configs, longer if you need VPC on-prem or dedicated networking.
09:47 James Li: ok. can you summarize what you'll send?
09:50 Lena Park: sure — SOC2 + security pack, Dedicated pricing scenarios, pilot credits details, benchmark script, and proposed dates.
09:57 Priya Menon: perfect. thanks everyone.
10:00 Meeting close.

Post-meeting notes (auto-generated):
- Customer is evaluation-first; prefer PLG quickstart to prove product with merchants before committing to Dedicated.
- Security team requires customer-managed KMS or Private deployment for a subset of merchants with strict residency.
- Pilot agreed: 90-day credits with focused 4-week active phase, benchmark scheduled for 2027-09-01.
- Action items assigned in metadata.

Notes on transcript quality: medium — some proper nouns (product names, model sizes) may be slightly off due to transcription artifacts.

References mentioned during call: Redwood security pack (link to be shared), pilot benchmark script (to be sent by Marco), Dedicated pricing scenarios (to be emailed).
